extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and others seeking guidance on USPTO IDS practice
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on what art/information must or may be submitted to the USPTO as an Information Disclosure Statement (IDS) during patent prosecution, the required contents and categories of listed art, who owes the duty to disclose, and how/when to submit an IDS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to disclose relevant art (duty of candor)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a duty on all patent applicants to disclose relevant art or background information that the applicant is aware of and that may be relevant to the patentability of the applicant's invention, as established by 35 U.S.C. and related sections of 37 CFR and the MPEP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The duty to submit such relevant information lies on the applicant/inventor and also on any patent attorney or other legal staff employed by the applicant. Failure to submit material prior art known to the applicant with deceptive intent can render any later-issued patent unenforceable because of inequitable conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of materials that may be submitted in an IDS
rubrics_metrics.description: The information submitted in an IDS typically includes other issued patents, published patent applications, scientific journal articles, books, magazine articles, or any other published material relevant to the invention disclosed in the applicant's patent application, irrespective of country or language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include any published material that may be relevant to patentability; unpublished or private information is not described here. The page emphasizes breadth of potentially relevant background art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories of art in an IDS
rubrics_metrics.description: Art listed on an IDS is typically broken up into three categories: U.S. patent literature, foreign patent literature, and non-patent literature (NPL).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: US patent literature: issued U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications. Foreign patent literature: patents issued in foreign countries, foreign application publications, and PCT international application publications. NPL: publications that are not U.S. or foreign patent publications (e.g., magazine articles, research journals).

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies required for listed documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of listed non‑patent literature (NPL) and foreign patent publications must be submitted with the IDS; copies of listed U.S. patent literature do not need to be submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO examiners have access to all U.S. patent literature, so copies of U.S. patents or U.S. patent publications are not required. If required copies of NPL or foreign patent publications are not provided, they will not be considered by USPTO examiners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation/summary requirement for non‑English documents
rubrics_metrics.description: If copies of NPL or foreign patent publications are not in the English language, the applicant must submit an English translation or a summary of relevancy in English for the piece of art to be considered by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Without an English translation or relevancy summary, a non‑English document submitted as part of an IDS will not be considered by the examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal effect of listing a reference in an IDS
rubrics_metrics.description: Art listed on an IDS, on its own, is not automatically considered prior art; mere listing of a reference in an IDS is not taken as an admission that the reference is prior art against the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listing does not equate to conceding that a reference is prior art; the examiner must still determine relevance and patentability effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content requirements governed by 37 CFR 1.98 (and MPEP)
rubrics_metrics.description: The content requirements of an IDS are defined in 37 CFR 1.98 and further explained in the MPEP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should consult 37 CFR 1.98 and the MPEP for the specific content rules (what information about each citation must be provided) when preparing an IDS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission requirements and timing governed by 37 CFR 1.97 (and MPEP)
rubrics_metrics.description: The submission requirements (when and how an IDS may be submitted) are defined in 37 CFR 1.97 and the MPEP; an IDS is not permitted in a provisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As of October 2006, relevant art may be submitted on paper using a USPTO-issued form or electronically via the USPTO electronic filing system. Applicants must follow the timing and procedural rules in 37 CFR 1.97 to ensure the IDS is considered.
